name: PSYC100 - Psychology (Comprehensive)
description: Social influence, professional psychology, and cognitive biases with detailed questions per lesson

lessons.title: W7L01: What makes us human?
lessons.description: Human nature and social psychology intro

lessons.title: W7L03: The power of the situation
W7L06: Why we lie to ourselves
W7L07: The power of the crowd
W7L08: Social influence in digital age
W7L10: Reflection - me vs the system
W9L01: The brain as shortcut machine

questions.question: What distinguishes human social behavior from other animals?
questions.explanation: Humans have unique capacity for culture, language, and abstract moral thinking

questions.question: What is social psychology primarily concerned with?
choices: How situations and others influence behavior
questions.answer: How situations and others influence behavior
questions.explanation: Social psychology studies how social context shapes thoughts and actions

questions.question: What makes humans particularly vulnerable to social influence?
questions.explanation: Social needs drive conformity and obedience

questions.question: In Milgram's experiment, what percentage of participants gave the maximum shock?
questions.explanation: Despite predictions of <1%, 65% obeyed to the maximum level

questions.question: What did Milgram's experiment demonstrate?
choices: People obey authority even when harming others
questions.answer: People obey authority even when harming others
questions.explanation: Ordinary people obeyed perceived authority to inflict harm

questions.question: What factor most increased obedience in Milgram's study?
questions.explanation: Proximity of authority increased compliance rates

questions.question: What is the fundamental attribution error?
questions.explanation: We attribute others' behavior to character while ignoring context
questions.lesson: W7L03: The power of the situation

questions.question: When we make mistakes, we tend to blame:
questions.explanation: We make the opposite error for ourselves vs others
questions.lesson: W7L03: The power of the situation

questions.question: What did Zimbardo's Stanford Prison Experiment show?
questions.explanation: Role assignment transformed normal people's behavior dramatically
questions.lesson: W7L03: The power of the situation

questions.question: In Asch's line study, what were participants asked to do?
choices: Match line lengths - an easy task
questions.answer: Match line lengths - an easy task
questions.explanation: Task was deliberately simple to highlight conformity pressure

questions.question: What percentage of Asch participants conformed at least once?
questions.explanation: About 75% went along with wrong answer at least once

questions.question: What reduces conformity in Asch's paradigm?
choices: Having one ally who disagrees with group
questions.answer: Having one ally who disagrees with group
questions.explanation: A single dissenter breaks the unanimity and reduces conformity

questions.question: What is the bystander effect?
choices: Less likely to help when others are present
questions.answer: Less likely to help when others are present
questions.explanation: More bystanders leads to diffusion of responsibility

questions.question: What is diffusion of responsibility?
choices: Feeling less personally responsible in groups
questions.answer: Feeling less personally responsible in groups
questions.explanation: Presence of others dilutes individual sense of obligation

questions.question: What case sparked research on the bystander effect?
questions.explanation: 38 witnesses reportedly didn't intervene in her murder

questions.question: What is cognitive dissonance?
questions.explanation: Tension from holding conflicting cognitions
questions.lesson: W7L06: Why we lie to ourselves

questions.question: How do people typically reduce cognitive dissonance?
questions.explanation: We rationalize to restore consistency
questions.lesson: W7L06: Why we lie to ourselves

questions.question: What is an example of cognitive dissonance?
choices: Smoker who knows smoking is unhealthy
questions.answer: Smoker who knows smoking is unhealthy
questions.explanation: Behavior contradicts knowledge, creating discomfort
questions.lesson: W7L06: Why we lie to ourselves

questions.question: What is groupthink?
choices: Desire for harmony leads to poor decisions
questions.answer: Desire for harmony leads to poor decisions
questions.explanation: Consensus-seeking overrides realistic appraisal
questions.lesson: W7L07: The power of the crowd

questions.question: What is group polarization?
choices: Groups become more extreme after discussion
questions.answer: Groups become more extreme after discussion
questions.explanation: Group discussion amplifies initial tendencies
questions.lesson: W7L07: The power of the crowd

questions.question: What is deindividuation?
questions.explanation: Anonymity in groups reduces personal responsibility
questions.lesson: W7L07: The power of the crowd

questions.question: How does social media amplify social influence?
questions.explanation: Algorithms create filter bubbles and rapid information cascade
questions.lesson: W7L08: Social influence in digital age

questions.question: What is an echo chamber?
questions.explanation: Exposure only to confirming information strengthens beliefs
questions.lesson: W7L08: Social influence in digital age

questions.question: What is a key ethical principle established after Milgram's study?
questions.explanation: Participants must know risks and be debriefed after

questions.question: What is the principle of 'do no harm' in research?
choices: Minimize risk and distress to participants
questions.answer: Minimize risk and distress to participants
questions.explanation: Benefits must outweigh risks, with protections in place

questions.question: What does the person-situation debate examine?
choices: Relative influence of personality vs context
questions.answer: Relative influence of personality vs context
questions.explanation: Behavior results from interaction of person and situation
questions.lesson: W7L10: Reflection - me vs the system

questions.question: What's the best predictor of behavior?
questions.explanation: Interactionist perspective: person × situation
questions.lesson: W7L10: Reflection - me vs the system

questions.question: What are the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy from bottom to top?
questions.explanation: Needs are hierarchical: lower must be met before higher

questions.question: According to Maslow, what must happen before seeking esteem?
questions.explanation: Hierarchy suggests progression from basic to higher needs

questions.question: What is self-actualization?
questions.explanation: Highest level: becoming the best version of yourself

questions.question: What are the three components of self-determination theory?
questions.explanation: These three psychological needs drive intrinsic motivation

questions.question: What is autonomy in SDT?
questions.explanation: Feeling self-directed rather than controlled

questions.question: What is relatedness in SDT?
questions.explanation: Sense of belonging and meaningful relationships

questions.question: What makes goals effective according to goal-setting theory?
questions.explanation: SMART goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound

questions.question: Why should goals be challenging but achievable?
questions.explanation: Sweet spot: stretches abilities without overwhelming

questions.question: What is self-efficacy?
choices: Belief in your ability to succeed at tasks
questions.answer: Belief in your ability to succeed at tasks
questions.explanation: Task-specific confidence in one's capabilities

questions.question: How does high self-efficacy affect behavior?
questions.explanation: Belief in success drives greater investment

questions.question: What is the difference between fixed and growth mindset?
choices: Fixed: abilities are unchangeable; Growth: abilities can develop
questions.answer: Fixed: abilities are unchangeable; Growth: abilities can develop
questions.explanation: Growth mindset sees intelligence as malleable through effort

questions.question: How do people with growth mindset view failure?
questions.explanation: Setbacks are feedback for improvement, not identity threats

questions.question: What is locus of control?
choices: Belief about who controls your outcomes
questions.answer: Belief about who controls your outcomes
questions.explanation: Internal vs external attribution of control

questions.question: What characterizes internal locus of control?
questions.explanation: Internal: success and failure come from own actions

questions.question: What is flow according to Csikszentmihalyi?
choices: Optimal experience when challenge matches skill
questions.answer: Optimal experience when challenge matches skill
questions.explanation: Total absorption in activity; in the zone

questions.question: What prevents flow?
choices: Challenge too high (anxiety) or too low (boredom)
questions.answer: Challenge too high (anxiety) or too low (boredom)
questions.explanation: Flow requires balance: skills match challenges

questions.question: What does ABCDE stand for in the stress model?
questions.explanation: Cognitive approach to managing stress and emotions

questions.question: What does the ABCDE model teach?
questions.explanation: Beliefs about events, not events themselves, cause distress

questions.question: What does JD-R model stand for?
questions.explanation: Model of workplace stress and motivation

questions.question: According to JD-R, what prevents burnout?
choices: Resources that match or exceed demands
questions.answer: Resources that match or exceed demands
questions.explanation: Sufficient resources buffer against high demands

questions.question: What is psychological safety?
choices: Feeling safe to take interpersonal risks
questions.answer: Feeling safe to take interpersonal risks
questions.explanation: Team climate where people can speak up without fear

questions.question: Why is psychological safety important?
choices: Enables learning, innovation, and honest feedback
questions.answer: Enables learning, innovation, and honest feedback
questions.explanation: People share ideas and admit mistakes without fear

questions.question: What is grit according to Angela Duckworth?
choices: Perseverance and passion for long-term goals
questions.answer: Perseverance and passion for long-term goals
questions.explanation: Sustained effort and interest over years

questions.question: What predicts success better than IQ according to grit research?
questions.explanation: Grit matters more than raw ability for achievement

questions.question: What is imposter syndrome?
choices: Feeling like a fraud despite accomplishments
questions.answer: Feeling like a fraud despite accomplishments
questions.explanation: Doubting deserved success, attributing it to luck

questions.question: Who commonly experiences imposter syndrome?
questions.explanation: Paradoxically common among accomplished individuals

questions.question: How do motivation theories connect to professional success?
questions.explanation: Applying psychological principles enhances performance

questions.question: Which combination predicts success?
questions.explanation: Believing in development, persisting, and trusting ability

questions.question: What are heuristics?
questions.explanation: Fast but sometimes flawed judgment strategies
questions.lesson: W9L01: The brain as shortcut machine

questions.question: Why does the brain use heuristics?
questions.explanation: Cognitive shortcuts save mental resources
questions.lesson: W9L01: The brain as shortcut machine

questions.question: What is the availability heuristic?
choices: Judging probability by ease of recall
questions.answer: Judging probability by ease of recall
questions.explanation: Memorable events seem more common than they are
questions.lesson: W9L01: The brain as shortcut machine

questions.question: What is anchoring bias?
questions.explanation: Initial values influence subsequent estimates

questions.question: What is framing effect?
choices: Same info presented differently affects choices
questions.answer: Same info presented differently affects choices
questions.explanation: 90% survival vs 10% mortality rate example

questions.question: Why does framing affect decisions?
choices: We're not purely rational - presentation matters
questions.answer: We're not purely rational - presentation matters
questions.explanation: Emotional response to framing overrides logic

questions.question: What is loss aversion in prospect theory?
choices: Losses hurt more than equivalent gains feel good
questions.answer: Losses hurt more than equivalent gains feel good
questions.explanation: Losing $100 > pain than gaining $100 = pleasure

questions.question: How do people behave differently in gain vs loss frames?
choices: Risk-averse for gains, risk-seeking for losses
questions.answer: Risk-averse for gains, risk-seeking for losses
questions.explanation: Gamble to avoid losses, play safe with gains

questions.question: What did Elizabeth Loftus discover about memory?
choices: Memories can be distorted and created by suggestion
questions.answer: Memories can be distorted and created by suggestion
questions.explanation: Leading questions create false memories that feel real

questions.question: What is the misinformation effect?
choices: Post-event information alters memory of original event
questions.answer: Post-event information alters memory of original event
questions.explanation: Later suggestions integrate into memory as if originally experienced

questions.question: What is inattentional blindness?
choices: Failing to notice obvious things when focused elsewhere
questions.answer: Failing to notice obvious things when focused elsewhere
questions.explanation: Gorilla walking through basketball game example

questions.question: What does selective attention demonstrate?
choices: Limited attentional capacity - can't process everything
questions.answer: Limited attentional capacity - can't process everything
questions.explanation: Attention is a limited resource; focus means missing other things

questions.question: What did the marshmallow test measure?
questions.explanation: Could children wait for bigger reward later?

questions.question: What did original marshmallow studies claim to predict?
questions.explanation: Self-control in childhood correlated with better outcomes (though debated)

questions.question: What is the Dunning-Kruger effect?
choices: Incompetent people overestimate ability; experts underestimate
questions.answer: Incompetent people overestimate ability; experts underestimate
questions.explanation: Lack of knowledge prevents recognizing lack of knowledge

questions.question: Why do novices overestimate their competence?
choices: They don't know what they don't know
questions.answer: They don't know what they don't know
questions.explanation: Metacognitive deficit: skill needed to judge skill is the skill itself

questions.question: How do emotions affect decision-making?
questions.explanation: Emotions are integral to decision-making, not just interference

questions.question: What are somatic markers?
choices: Bodily emotional signals that guide choices
questions.answer: Bodily emotional signals that guide choices
questions.explanation: Gut feelings based on past emotional experiences

questions.question: What is the halo effect?
choices: One positive trait makes us view everything positively
questions.answer: One positive trait makes us view everything positively
questions.explanation: Attractive = assumed smart, kind, competent

questions.question: What is the horn effect?
choices: One negative trait makes us view everything negatively
questions.answer: One negative trait makes us view everything negatively
questions.explanation: Opposite of halo: single flaw taints overall impression

questions.question: What do cognitive biases reveal about human thinking?
choices: We're predictably irrational in systematic ways
questions.answer: We're predictably irrational in systematic ways
questions.explanation: Biases are consistent patterns, not random errors

questions.question: Can awareness of biases eliminate them?
choices: No, but can reduce impact with strategies
questions.answer: No, but can reduce impact with strategies
questions.explanation: Awareness helps but doesn't eliminate automatic biases
